title: Isometric Game
description: An ongoing project inspired by Polytopia, SimCity, and Civ VI. Built both 2D and isometric prototypes, implemented pathfinding and world saving. I plan to restart the project in C++ with better architecture and devlogs.

title: MNIST Neural Network
description: For my high school capstone, I decided to learn fully connected neural networks by creating one from scratch. Along the way I learned how forward and backward propagation actually work. I trained it to classify hand-drawn digits using the MNIST dataset.

title: Bezier Curve Swerve Paths
description: A tool to generate smooth autonomous paths for our FIRST Robotics team's swerve drive using Bezier curves. Helped us win the Autonomous Award at the Arizona East 2023 Regional.

title: WikiFacts AI Video Project
description: An automated pipeline that generated short videos summarizing articles into 5 facts. The project I used to get familiar with working with LLM APIs. It used ChatGPT, Wikipedia, Google Images, Amazon TTS, and OpenCV to compile videos and upload to YouTube Shorts. Gained over 150K+ views.

title: TapTech Studio
description: An NFC products company I run. I create personalized 3D-printed keychains, each with an NFC URL that its owner could point at their LinkedIn or favorite Spotify playlist.

title: Abstract Wave Art
description: I was super inspired by water caustics and wave patterns when I decided to create this project. It layers and rotates a mathematical wave (e^sin(x)), using its derivative for shadows, to generate light maps. I shared some of the generative art results on an Instagram page.

title: MechVolta
description: My first Luminosity Lab project, freshman year: storing electricity mechanically in using motors, springs and a generator.

title: Gravitational Physics Sim
description: A JavaFX simulation modeling orbital physics using Newton's law of gravitation. I built it for honors credit in my programming and physics classes, and it led to a spot in the Photoemission and Bright Beams lab.

title: SabL-Cesium
description: A conceptual system of universal measurement units not based on Earth-centric standards like the second or meter.

title: ESP32 Websocket Car
description: I designed this car that hosts a website on an ESP32. The website allows you to control the car using a keyboard on any device on the same network. Modeled, printed, wired and programmed solo in C, used a websocket for low latency controls.

title: Mini CHARLOTTE
description: I designed this robot using the CHARLOTTE robot as a reference. The original CHARLOTTE was made for the NASA Big Idea Competition in 2022, and won the Systems Engineering Award. Mini CHARLOTTE is fully 3D-printed, uses a Raspberry Pi and 12 Robotis motors to control the 3 3DOF legs, and the 3 1DOF legs.

title: Toolboard
description: One board for all the little tools you use on a project, like a to-do list, a calendar or your links, laid out as cards. This repo is the original version; the newer one in TypeScript is private for now.

title: Prompter
description: An experiment in measuring prompts. It changes a prompt in small ways, like swapping words, and measures the effect on the output, to see what actually makes a prompt work.

title: Pantry
description: An iOS pantry inventory app, live on the App Store. Features barcode and receipt scanning with a database of 400k+ food items. Expiration reminders, meal suggestions, macro tracking and a lot more. Uses RevenueCat subscriptions and a Supabase backend, hosted on my VPS along with my other projects.

title: Orbitscape
description: A space mission visualization platform I co-lead at the Luminosity Lab, now launched as a startup with a twelve-person team.

title: Particle Analyzer
description: A Luminosity Lab device that charges particles and then detects them, measuring their size and other properties. I worked on the CAD, and learned to design parts for machining in metal rather than 3D printing.

title: Project Jude
description: A lifesaving submarine device at the Luminosity Lab. I did the CAD for the first version and now advise the team building the next one.

title: Zipper: Discord AI Assistant
description: An AI personal assistant running on my VPS. The first iterations were built for the purpose of building itself, recently it has become a self-upadating knowledge graph, it injests information from various inputs to keep the notes current, send me reminders and keep a todo list always up to date.

title: Voussoir
description: A referral-code marketplace concept. Everyone earns the ability to post referral links by using other people's links, basically inducing demand.

title: Iron Man Helmet
description: A 500-feature surface-modeled Iron Man helmet created in Onshape and printed on my Bambu P1S. Learned surface modeling just for this project, then motorized it with servos and an ESP32.

title: GIFs Against Humanity
description: A party game where the answers are GIFs. Everyone plays on their own phone, with an optional TV as the shared screen. No accounts or downloads: open the site, type a four-letter code, pick a nickname.

title: Barrett Thesis
description: My honors thesis: designing a low-cost, open-ended STEM kit and coding curriculum for an under-resourced classroom, with a school in Kenya as the main deployment site.

title: Procedural Pixel Art Trees
description: I'm bad at pixel art, so I wrote a program to create art automatically. Inspired by real binary trees, I turned it into a graphic and grew random trees with growing animations. Every tree in this forest is grown by this algorithm.

title: TileWorld
description: A top-down pygame world that generates itself in chunks as you walk: grassland and forest from my own pixel-art tiles, with menus, separate save files for each world, and tiles you can build on. The grass in this forest comes from it.

title: Stonkle
description: A stock-guessing game. You see the first three months of a random stock's chart, and choose buy or sell. The the next three months are revealed and you score points for being right, levelling up as you go.

title: Bit Tic-Tac-Toe
description: A command-line tic-tac-toe in C++ where each player's moves are stored as a 9-bit number. Checking for a win is just ANDing those bits against the eight winning patterns, so it's very fast.
